coordinate_system.orientation_notes: The front and lug-detail projections lie in XY, with +X right and +Y up. Z is the central rotational and axial machining direction. Adopt +Z from the datum A front face toward the rear annular face, consistent with the face access directions in section A-A. Section A-A has Y vertical, Z horizontal and X as its cut normal. Use the datum B axis for the radial center and datum C for angular orientation where explicitly referenced; angular orientation for controls referencing C-C remains unresolved.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: The position controls in detail Z specify A as primary, B as secondary and C-C as tertiary. Detail Y separately specifies A then C for surface profile, and A for perpendicularity. Datum C-C has no definition in the supplied graphs and is not assumed equivalent to datum C or to the section cut C-C; its datum-reference edges remain unresolved. Datum C is represented by the tooth-sector feature carrying its radial center-plane reference, not by a separately invented planar feature.

assumptions.text: The main-view and isometric external-lug observations are treated as aggregate observations of the outer lug family. Their counterparts in U, V, W and X remain separate because the parent leaders identify different locations and the toleranced widths differ. Each detail is canonical for its own profile; the shared aggregate observations do not create standalone nodes or determine instance counts.

Detail U's explicit tenfold qualifiers are retained as supplied, not redistributed to V, W or X and not added to other counts to infer a total. Their applicability where the other detail widths differ is unresolved and is addressed by C01.

Detail Z's five-lug feature is not merged with the outer ten-lug observations despite the broad detail Z reference on front_view:F3. Its distinct envelope, multiplicity and spatial zone show that the detail circle covers geometry beyond that outer-lug observation.

The root cylinders in U, V, W and X are grouped on Signal 5: matching feature type, identical toleranced radius from the common part center and consistent supporting-root context. Detail W is canonical because it supplies both radius and diameter and identifies the cylindrical axis consistently with the projection notes.

The main-view root cylinder is provisionally retained as a separate singleton from the U–X root group. Its nominal and tolerance do not reconcile with the detail radius by diameter conversion, and the supplied sections do not establish whether these are different axial surfaces. No conflicting value is silently selected.

The detail Y pocket is merged with detail_z:F4 using the explicit Y callout on that feature and the section-level Y callout around the roller-stop pocket. Detail Z is canonical for its more extensive dimensional definition and explicit radius tolerance; detail Y contributes its profile, perpendicularity, straightness and finish controls.

Datum C is associated with detail_y:F2 as the carrier of the radial tooth/pocket-sector center plane. Both Y features reference that plane, but the pocket contact-circle center is explicitly offset from it. No new datum-surface node is invented.
Datum C-C is left undefined rather than equated with datum C or the identically named section cut. Relationships to that unknown datum are withheld pending C03.

isometric_view:F1 and isometric_view:F2 remain ungrouped pictorial observations. The body observation spans several separately defined surfaces, and the generic internal spline observation cannot be identified confidently with one particular internal land, slot or tooth feature. No standard spline specification is inferred from its descriptive name.

The B-B and C-C edge observations remain distinct singletons. Matching dimensions on opposing edges do not establish identity, and the supplied cut references do not identify a unique dimensioned parent profile for attaching them.

Overall ring thickness and counterbore depth are not automatically assigned as axial extents of every lug or internal profile. Those lengths would be arithmetically derivable once the relevant front and rear termination surfaces are confirmed; C04 and C05 ask for that missing geometric relationship rather than for redundant dimensions.

The tenfold requirement (10x 14.8±0.1) in Detail U applies exclusively to the 10 standard lugs of that configuration and does not apply to Details V, W, and X. The lugs in Details V, W, and X represent distinct individual features governed by their own independently specified widths of 17.8±0.1 mm, 14±0.1 mm, and 12.8±0.1 mm, respectively.

Yes, the R93.3 root contours in details U–X represent the same continuous cylindrical root surface dimensioned as Ø187.2±0.15 in the main view. They are assumed to be the same physical feature, with Ø187.2 defining the overall root diameter between the outer lugs.
Datum C-C is established by the 14 mm wide internal slot (notch/keyway) dimensioned 5x 14±0.1 on the inner diameter, whose opposing side faces define the datum center plane.

The external lug profiles and their flank reliefs in details U–X are assumed to extend continuously across the full axial distance between datum A and the rear annular face, as no intermediate axial stop or terminating depth is indicated.

The circumferential cam profiles shown in details Z and Y extend continuously along the full axial length from the front counterbore shoulder to the rear annular face without interruptions or undercuts.

The B-B shoulder fillet and edge treatments are required at all external lug locations, encompassing all 10 lugs defined in Detail U as well as the individual lugs defined in Details V, W, and X (13 lugs total). The R93.3±0.2 shoulder radius and corresponding edge geometries are explicitly defined across all four detail views.
The section C-C chamfers apply to the five internal radial lugs (pads), which are dimensioned with a width of 14 ± 0.1 mm and an inner diameter of Ø154.6 +0.05/0 mm (Datum B).
